propositions: Source code comments contain rot-prone historical references (commit SHAs, run/job/thread IDs, dated incident narratives) that become unresolvable due to version control rebasing and log retention windows; 16+ sites identified at HEAD with unresolvable citations

A new block-level detector (check_comment_hygiene.py) must scan for rot-prone patterns (SHA-like hex ≥7 chars, run IDs ≥8 digits, date+incident-verb pairs) and accept only blocks citing durable ticket/epic/story/bug/ADR IDs or bearing 'context: external' escape hatch

All detector-hit sites must be remediated by one of three methods: cite a resolvable ticket-system ID, drop the rot-prone token leaving durable prose, or replace SHA narratives with behavioral descriptions findable via git log

The CI guard must be integrated into .github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml as a named step following the check_*.py convention, with tests/unit/test_comment_hygiene_guard.py covering FP gotchas (word-triple aliases in path context, 'bug surfaced' without incident dates) and acceptor rules (4x4-grouped and word-triple IDs must accept; sentence-final aliases must accept)

Post-remediation tree scans must pass with zero in-tree escape-hatch uses, and policy guidance must be added to CONTRIBUTING.md establishing that source code is for current state and concise rationale while tickets own historical detail
